chapter: Looking back and the lean years
title: Moving to Washington for the Blues Alley house-band job
summary: The owner promises a steady house-band job, he rents an apartment, and then learns the club is for sale.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Do you want to tell the story about moving to Washington; I think that's another example.
Well, yes - that's a good example. I was at Blues Alley and the guy in the Blues Alley said - well, he said, I'd like to do something with you -- he said, I'd like to have you have the band here.

You have the house band and I'll give you a steady job and then we'll bring in all the stars and you can back them up; That - I bit for that one because a steady job was few and far between. So, I went up there as you know, and I went there; I rented a gorgeous apartment - fixed it all up - and everything - the first couple of weeks went by - everything was cool and then, suddenly, I hear rumors around the place that they had the place up for sale. So, I told him one night--- I said, what the hell are you doing? Oh, he says, he said - this is really too much for me here; I'm going to sell this place; I said - why the hell didn't you tell me that before you got me up here -- you know -- things that were --- these were things that were happening to me. I'm sure it was happening to many others, certainly not just me because I wasn't the only musician that was jobbing around and I certainly wasn't the only musician that was trying to keep bands together---
And, he did ultimately sell the place--
